items.label: Virtual water in 1,000 g of jeans, global average

components.text: The two are counted differently, one over a pair's whole life, one as virtual water per kilogram. Read them side by side, never added or ranked

footnote: Source: Levi Strauss & Co., The Life Cycle of a Jean (2015), Chapagain et al., The water footprint of cotton consumption (2005)
notes: There are at least two ways to count the water in a pair of jeans, and I keep them side by side rather than merging them. On the left is Levi's own 2015 life cycle assessment of one stonewashed 501: 3,781 litres of net water use, 68% of it in growing the cotton. That is the company's figure. On the right is a 2005 virtual water study: for 1,000 grams of jeans, a global average of 10,850 litres, which also counts rainwater and the water needed to dilute pollution. A larger figure that circulates online comes with no method, so I left it out. And to be clear, both numbers describe the cost of a new pair of jeans. Neither is water this collection saved.
